title: Gleisdreieck Berlin - FAQ
subtitle: The station, the park, the house the train runs through and when to go.

items.a: It means **track triangle**. When Berlin's elevated railway opened in **1902**, three branches met here in a triangle of tracks. After a collision in **1908**, the junction was rebuilt into a two-level crossing station, but the name stayed.

items.q: Which U-Bahn lines stop at Gleisdreieck?
items.a: The **U1 and U3** stop in the upper hall and the **U2** in the lower hall. You change between them on a cross of staircases inside the station.

items.q: Is Park am Gleisdreieck free and open at night?
items.a: Yes. The park is free and open **day and night**. It opened in stages: the Ostpark in **2011**, the Westpark in **2013** and the southern strip, now Dora-Duncker-Park, in **2014**.

items.q: Where does the U-Bahn run through a house in Berlin?
items.a: At **Dennewitzstraße 2**, on the corner of Pohlstraße, just west of Park am Gleisdreieck. The house was rebuilt in **1925 and 1926** so the line could pass through it. It carries the **U1 and U3**, not the U2.

items.q: How long does a walk around Gleisdreieck take?
items.a: About **an hour** on foot for the station, the viaduct, the house, the rail relics, the Yorckbrücken and the Candy Bomber. Add three hours or more if you visit the Technikmuseum.

items.q: Is the Technikmuseum open on Mondays?
items.a: No, the German Museum of Technology is **closed on Mondays**. From 3 November 2026 to 28 March 2027 its Museum Park closes at **16:00**, so in winter visit the museum early in the day.

items.q: What is the plane on the Technikmuseum?
items.a: It is a **Douglas C-47**, one of the Candy Bombers that flew supplies into West Berlin during the **1948 to 1949** blockade. It hangs above the museum terrace near the Landwehrkanal, and you can see it from the street without a ticket.
